hypothesis: A large household/macroeconomic shock should mechanically exhaust bank credit-loss buffers.
evidence: Net irregular private-credit exposure was -3.5% PN pre and -2.9% in Jun/Dec-2014.
interpretation: Bank credit-loss buffers were not saturated even though other bank/household outcomes moved.

hypothesis: The deep 2018 household drawdown required a comparable depletion of bank net worth through private-credit losses.
evidence: Net exposure was only 1.3% PN in Nov and 1.6% in Dec-2018; by Mar-2019 uncovered irregular credit was <10% of excess regulatory capital.
interpretation: Household stress and bank credit-risk capital use can be highly asymmetric.

hypothesis: End-2017 vs end-2018 exposure/PN change measures pure stress-buffer use.
evidence: Initial NIIF adoption increased system PN 14.8% vs end-2017, mainly property revaluation.
interpretation: Use 2018 within-regime levels, not a naive 2017→2018 delta.

hypothesis: The 2023 bank capital buffer was close to saturation by credit risk.
evidence: BCRA extreme low-probability stress exercises move capital position 289→283 and 289→272% of requirement.
interpretation: Credit-risk solvency buffer remained far from the regulatory minimum under modeled severe shocks.

hypothesis: Normative unemployment/CBA coverage directly identifies how much household shock was absorbed.
evidence: V43 has ceilings/formulas and transfer/CBA coverage, but not claimant prior-wage loss or household counterfactual income.
interpretation: Household stress-use remains N/D pending administrative/microdata evidence.

hypothesis: There is one immutable official 2013 provision-coverage number.
evidence: Official vintages report 140.2%, 147.8%, and later historical values ~148/150 depending definition/publication.
interpretation: Preserve reporting vintage and denominator; do not silently harmonize.
